title: Composite Sickles and Cereal Harvesting Methods at 23,000-Years-Old Ohalo II, Israel
lineage: Publisher version. The five blades constitute different specimens from the Ohalo II grains and grinding slab analyzed in earlier studies by overlapping teams.

passages.note: Cutting wear on five flint blades resembles experimental wear from cutting near-ripe cereal stems. Two blades, AL73c and AJ39c, carry wear interpreted as evidence of hafting.
Most recovered grains were fully ripe. The excavated grain assemblage need not be the harvest represented by these tools.
